x: Although most of our "cracks" were barred from this race, we fielded a useful team, our chief rivals being Reading A.C., who included in their team F.

Reeve, of the Poly., once again beat Bill Lucas into second place, but as the time was 4 min. 25 sec., and Frank Close finished third, I think Lucas has every reason to be pleased at his fine running.
Mortimer, that very promising young Finchley Harrier. Our side had been strengthened by the inclusion of Frank Close, the well known miler and International runner; also A.
Wilson, of the Polytechnic, beat Frank Close in the 1 Mile, but a club mate of the latter, J.

Bedford, a new member, ran well in the 880 Yards race to finish second, and he also gained third place in the 1 Mile, in which Frank Close, the International runner, made a re-appearance to gain second place.
